profile.summary: A small coffee shop near the UMD campus with 6 mostly student employees, struggling with semester-based shift scheduling, dormant Instagram, and slow weekday afternoons.

raw_pains.title: Spending about 4 hours a week redoing schedules and texting people to cover shifts
raw_pains.owner_quote: spend like 4 hours a week just redoing the schedule and texting people to cover shifts

raw_pains.title: Instagram has been dead for months
raw_pains.owner_quote: Our Instagram has been dead for months because I don't have time to post

raw_pains.title: Weekday afternoons from 2 to 5 are very slow
raw_pains.owner_quote: Afternoons between 2 and 5 are super slow on weekdays and I'd love to get students in then

facts.object: coffee shop near the UMD campus

data.label: Putting a dollar figure on each pain

pains.title: Redoing schedules each semester and texting staff to cover shifts
pains.impact_explanation: 4 hrs/wk of owner time at ~$45/hr is about $180/wk, or roughly $780/mo, in time alone. Shift gaps can also leave the counter short during rushes, but that is hard to quantify without data.
pains.evidence_quote: spend like 4 hours a week just redoing the schedule and texting people to cover shifts

pains.title: Weekday 2-5pm traffic is very slow
pains.impact_explanation: Assume the 2-5pm weekday window runs about 10 empty transactions per day at a $6 average ticket across 5 weekdays: 10 x $6 x 5 x 4.3 weeks = ~$1,290/mo of capacity. Winning back roughly 2-3 extra customers per day with a student-targeted offer is a conservative ~$700-900/mo.
pains.evidence_quote: Afternoons between 2 and 5 are super slow on weekdays and I'd love to get students in then

pains.title: Instagram has been dead for months
pains.impact_explanation: Owner would spend ~1.5 hrs/wk creating and posting content (~$290/mo in time). Lost discovery from a dormant account is hard to measure, but a conservative ~$300/mo in lost walk-ins from campus followers is plausible.
pains.evidence_quote: Our Instagram has been dead for months because I don't have time to post

data.label: Scouting tools for “Redoing schedules each semester and texting staff to cover shifts”
Scouting tools for “Weekday 2-5pm traffic is very slow”
Scouting tools for “Instagram has been dead for months”

picks.why_fit: Builds schedules automatically from sales forecasts and includes a shift trade app so staff can swap shifts without the owner texting around, and it integrates directly with square-pos which Joe's already uses.
picks.estimate_reasoning: The 4 hrs/wk pain is mostly schedule building plus coverage texting. Auto-scheduling and the shift trade app should remove most of both tasks, though the owner still needs to review schedules and approve swaps, so about 0.7 is a realistic share. No revenue at risk was quantified, so pct_revenue_recovered is 0.

picks.why_fit: Offers auto-scheduling, team chat and a time clock for hourly teams, with a free tier and an integration with square-pos, so it fits Joe's budget and existing POS.
picks.estimate_reasoning: Auto-scheduling and team chat reduce both the schedule rebuild and the coverage texting, but the team chat is less specialized for shift trades than 7shifts, so the estimate is a bit lower. Revenue impact is not quantified in the pain, so it is 0.

picks.why_fit: It is built into Square POS, which Joe's already uses, and offers auto win-back messages and a loyalty program that can target a student-focused offer for weekday afternoons using the real customer list.
picks.estimate_reasoning: The pain is about recovering weekday 2-5pm traffic, not hours, so time savings are minimal. Revenue recovery is estimated at roughly half of the $900/mo at risk, since a targeted afternoon offer to a student list plausibly wins back 2-3 customers per day, but the shop only has an existing list of unknown size and the offer must be well executed. Price is about $45/mo, within the $150 budget, and setup is about 1 hour.

picks.why_fit: Its free tier and AI email writer plus automated journeys let Joe's send a recurring student afternoon promo without paying much, and it integrates with Square.
picks.estimate_reasoning: Mailchimp can run the same afternoon offer campaign, but it lacks Square's native POS-linked loyalty and redemption tracking, so recovery is lower than the Square option. The free tier keeps cost near zero, leaving budget headroom. Realistic recovery is about 0.35 of the $900/mo at risk given list-building needs and weaker attribution to in-store visits.

picks.why_fit: Free Instagram scheduling plus AI-generated post text and AI inbox auto-replies lets the owner batch a week of posts in one sitting at zero cost, fitting the $150 budget and tech comfort of 3.
picks.estimate_reasoning: Scheduling and AI copy cut the ~1.5 hrs/week of posting to roughly 30-40 minutes of batching, removing about 60% of the time pain. Revenue recovery is moderate because it only reaches Instagram, which is the sole channel lost, and discovery from campus followers depends on posting consistency.

picks.why_fit: Magic Design templates and Magic Write copy let the owner produce on-brand coffee and menu visuals quickly, and the content planner handles scheduling to Instagram, which is already in use.
picks.estimate_reasoning: Templates remove the design step, which is a large share of posting time, but the owner still reviews and schedules, so about 45% of the time pain is removed. Revenue recovery is smaller since visuals help engagement but the scheduler is basic and less reliable for consistent posting.

critiques.concern: Its price climbs with list size, so a student list that grows each semester can quietly push you past $20/mo. Read the contact-tier pricing before you commit.

critiques.suggestion: Use one recurring weekly template so posting becomes a 20-minute habit, and batch-schedule with Meta Business Suite to avoid daily logins.

verdicts.summary: This stack fixes your three biggest headaches: messy student schedules, quiet weekday afternoons, and an Instagram account that has gone silent. It costs about $80 a month, well under your $150 budget, and should save around 16 hours a month while bringing back sales.

by_tool.7shifts: 7shifts should pay for itself in about 7 days and save you roughly 12 hours a month on building schedules and texting around for coverage. The main catch is that your student staff must actually use the app, so show them how at a shift meeting and make app swaps the only way to trade shifts.
by_tool.square-marketing: Square Marketing & Loyalty should pay back in about 4 days by winning students back into the shop on weekday afternoons. The main catch is that at $45 a month it takes up almost a third of your budget, so start with a simple targeted offer and check that it brings people in.
by_tool.meta-business-suite: Meta Business Suite is free and should pay back in under 5 days, since it lets you plan a week of Instagram posts in one sitting and saves about 4 hours a month. The advisors raised no concerns, though results depend on you posting steadily.

plan.first_step_today: Create a free 7shifts account and invite your 6 staff by email or text so they can enter their fall class availability this week.

tasks.text: Sign up for 7shifts, add Joe's Corner Coffee location, set opening hours and roles (barista, cashier, opener/closer)
Invite all 6 employees and ask each to enter class-schedule availability in the app by Friday
Connect 7shifts to Square POS if offered, otherwise skip and note typical busy hours from Square reports
Help staff who have trouble installing the app and confirm everyone has logged in

weeks.theme: Go live with the schedule, start the afternoon offer

tasks.text: Build next week's schedule from submitted availability and publish it; tell staff shift swaps now happen in the app, not by text
Turn on Square Marketing and Loyalty, and import existing customers from Square POS
Create a loyalty reward and a 2-5pm weekday student offer (e.g. $1 off any drink with student ID)
Train counter staff to mention the afternoon offer and sign customers up for loyalty at checkout

weeks.theme: Promote the offer and restart Instagram

tasks.text: Send one email or text campaign to customers about the 2-5pm student offer
Connect Instagram to Meta Business Suite and set up the content scheduler
Have a student employee take 8-10 photos/videos of drinks, the shop, and the afternoon offer during a slow shift
Schedule 3 posts for the week (offer, a drink feature, a team shot) in one sitting; repeat weekly
Publish the next schedule and approve any shift swaps in the app

weeks.theme: Measure results and decide what to keep

tasks.text: Estimate time spent on scheduling and shift-cover texts this week and compare to the old 4 hrs/wk
Check Square reports for 2-5pm weekday transactions and loyalty sign-ups vs. before the offer
Review Instagram post reach, follower growth, and profile visits in Meta Business Suite
Hold a 15-minute team huddle to gather feedback and decide what to adjust or keep for month two

success_metrics.metric: Owner hours per week on scheduling and shift-cover texts
success_metrics.target: Down from 4 hrs to 1 hr or less by week 4
2-3 more per day than the pre-offer baseline
50+ customers enrolled by end of week 4
3 posts per week for weeks 3 and 4

by_tool.meta-business-suite: Meta Business Suite is free and should pay back in under 5 days, since it lets you plan a week of Instagram posts in one sitting and saves about 4 hours a month. The advisors raised no concerns, though results depend on you posting steadily.

plan.first_step_today: Create a free 7shifts account and invite your 6 staff by email or text so they can enter their fall class availability this week.

tasks.text: Sign up for 7shifts, add Joe's Corner Coffee location, set opening hours and roles (barista, cashier, opener/closer)
Invite all 6 employees and ask each to enter class-schedule availability in the app by Friday
Connect 7shifts to Square POS if offered, otherwise skip and note typical busy hours from Square reports
Help staff who have trouble installing the app and confirm everyone has logged in

weeks.theme: Go live with the schedule, start the afternoon offer

tasks.text: Build next week's schedule from submitted availability and publish it; tell staff shift swaps now happen in the app, not by text
Turn on Square Marketing and Loyalty, and import existing customers from Square POS
Create a loyalty reward and a 2-5pm weekday student offer (e.g. $1 off any drink with student ID)
Train counter staff to mention the afternoon offer and sign customers up for loyalty at checkout

weeks.theme: Promote the offer and restart Instagram

tasks.text: Send one email or text campaign to customers about the 2-5pm student offer
Connect Instagram to Meta Business Suite and set up the content scheduler
Have a student employee take 8-10 photos/videos of drinks, the shop, and the afternoon offer during a slow shift
Schedule 3 posts for the week (offer, a drink feature, a team shot) in one sitting; repeat weekly
Publish the next schedule and approve any shift swaps in the app

weeks.theme: Measure results and decide what to keep

tasks.text: Estimate time spent on scheduling and shift-cover texts this week and compare to the old 4 hrs/wk
Check Square reports for 2-5pm weekday transactions and loyalty sign-ups vs. before the offer
Review Instagram post reach, follower growth, and profile visits in Meta Business Suite
Hold a 15-minute team huddle to gather feedback and decide what to adjust or keep for month two

success_metrics.metric: Owner hours per week on scheduling and shift-cover texts
success_metrics.target: Down from 4 hrs to 1 hr or less by week 4
2-3 more per day than the pre-offer baseline
50+ customers enrolled by end of week 4
3 posts per week for weeks 3 and 4
